subject: Re: MedTechCo — service holdback & deferred buyout structure
messages:
From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@medtech.co>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedTechCo Legal <legal@medtech.co>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Service holdback + deferred buyout proposal

Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the SLA draft and we have two non-negotiables we'd like to see in the agreement to move forward this quarter: an operational holdback (escrow) of a portion of monthly fees to be released only after a 30‑day post-incident verification period, and a deferred buyout mechanism if service quality degrades repeatedly.

High level asks: 
- 15% of monthly committed fees placed in escrow and releasable after a 30‑day remediation validation for any P1 incident.
- Right to terminate for cause with a buyout equal to 6 months of committed spend if we see 3 P1s in any rolling 90‑day window.
- If Redwood disputes a P1 classification, escrow continues to hold funds pending an independent post‑mortem (we can suggest a neutral third party).

I attached redlines to our SLA and an SOW that sketches the escrow mechanics. We can be flexible on timing but cannot accept credits-only remedies for repeated, production-impacting outages.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these constructs or propose a counter-structure that gives us an analogous economic safety net?

Thanks,
Sara Bloom
Dir., IT Ops — MedTechCo
Attachments: MedTech_SLA_Redlines.pdf, MedTech_ESCROW_SOW.xlsx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@medtech.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Service holdback + deferred buyout proposal

Sara —

Appreciate the clarity and the redlines. Short answer: we understand the need for stronger economic levers when an outage materially impacts your clinical workflows, but the specific construct you proposed (15% escrow + 6‑month buyout on 3 P1s/90d) is more punitive than our standard framework.

A few clarifying Qs so we don't go in circles:
1) Are the P1s you referenced strictly latency/availability (i.e., hard service outages) or do they include degraded quality (e.g., incorrect model responses) as well?
2) Is the 6‑month buyout intended to be payable immediately upon termination or amortized?
3) Would you consider an independent post‑mortem panel limited to classification disputes only (not re‑litigation of remedies)?

Initial counter-proposal we can put in an upcoming redline: 
- A stepped holdback: 10% of the monthly committed fee held as a short-duration reserve (released monthly unless a verified P1 occurs).
- Tiered remediation schedule: first P1 → 20% credit of that month's fees + 30‑day cure; second P1 within 90 days → additional one‑time fee-at-risk equal to 1.5x monthly committed fees moved to escrow; third P1 within 90 days → termination right with a capped buyout equal to 3x monthly committed fees.
- Escrow release tied to a mutually agreed verification POA; classification disputes handled by a single neutral engineer review (both parties agree).

This preserves a path to termination but caps the customer's cash outlay and gives us a reasonable cure process. If Marissa/legal think we should avoid granular step amounts in the SLA text, we can put exact tranches into an SOW addendum.

Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
From: MedTechCo Legal <legal@medtech.co>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Service holdback + deferred buyout proposal

Vivek / team —

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple points from legal: 
- The buyout amount should be sufficient to cover our migration and validation costs if we exit under duress; 3x monthly may still be below our threshold depending on integration spend.
- We want escrow mechanics codified (who holds the funds, release triggers, dispute timeline).
- Neutral reviewer needs to be from an agreed panel (not a single company-selected engineer).

We uploaded suggested language in the attached PDF. We are amenable to a stepped cure, but the economic progression should make it meaningfully painful to remain on a degraded service (credits alone won't deter risk to patients).

If you prefer, we can run a short statement-of-work draft that defines the escrow trustee, trigger events, and funds flow so the SLA can reference the SOW.

Regards,
MedTechCo Legal Team
Attachments: MedTech_SLA_Redlines.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@medtech.co>, MedTechCo Legal <legal@medtech.co>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Service holdback + deferred buyout proposal — internal negotiation plan

Team — forwarding Sara and Legal's asks. Key negotiation levers I propose we use to land a deal while protecting Redwood's financial exposure: 

1) Move from a flat 15% holdback to a time‑bounded reserve (10%) that auto-releases monthly except when a verified P1 is open; provides MedTech the economic buffer while keeping our cashflow predictable.

2) Convert a straight 6‑month buyout into a capped, stepwise buyout: 1x monthly after 2 P1s in 90d (with longer cure), 3x monthly after 3 P1s (shorter cure window). This produces escalation with clear remediation windows.

3) Offer an agreed neutral panel for P1 classification (3 members: 1 from MedTech, 1 from Redwood, 1 neutral agreed vendor). Panel decisions are binding for escrow release only.

4) Operational mitigations we should commit to: dedicated on-call for MedTech during first 90 days of production, weekly health exports to a shared dashboard, and a joint runbook for incident validation to speed root cause identification. These reduce the chance of protracted disputes.

5) Keep absolute dollar caps in the SOW rather than the SLA text — legal tends to accept a reference to the SOW for numeric tranches.

If you agree, Marissa/legal: can you draft short fallbacks for the SOW and a DocuSign-ready clause we can share with MedTech this afternoon? I'll propose the neutral panel language to them and ask for acceptance on the 10% holdback.

— Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
